correspondence.component_scope: Chosen southwestern opening and first eastward creek approach
correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies on the small eastward creek corridor southwest of Montagne Soufflet. The original map depicts the opening, its eastward bends and the connected approach to the named Crique Brodel reach. The first selected vertex is not treated as an official source or a separately named spring. Unlabeled initial subreaches remain unnamed.

correspondence.component_scope: Crique Brodel and its northeastward receiving-channel connection
correspondence.finding: The original headward map prints crique brodel along the selected east-to-northeast creek. The mapped blue watercourse continues around the southern and eastern side of the Montagne Soufflet setting and joins the larger northward receiving corridor. Crique La Folie and Crique Blanche are separately depicted branches; their labels are not transferred to the selected opening. The named Brodel component is bounded to this headward approach.

correspondence.component_scope: Upper northward receiving trunk and first fragment join
correspondence.finding: The selected river continues north and northeast along a continuously mapped, widening river valley, past the separate Roche Fendé-side drainage setting and into the Sainte-Anne/Étienne upper Comté corridor. The overlapping head and middle originals cover the entire intervening valley and the FID11513/11514 join. The named Comté receiving trunk is distinguished from the earlier Brodel creek; no exact naming-transition vertex is asserted.

correspondence.component_scope: Comté from the upper settled valley through Saut Bief and Cacao
correspondence.finding: The middle original labels Rivière Comté and shows its continuous corridor through the Bagot/Grand Bassin surroundings, Saut Bief, Cacao and Sainte-Anne. The selected generalized line cuts across some river bends and the Cacao settlement-side curve but stays within this same river corridor. Monfort and Ruf independently identify Saut Bief as a station on the Comté within the Mahury basin. The modeled segment is not substituted for the individual source-map meanders.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle and lower Comté bends to Saint-Régis
correspondence.finding: North of Cacao the selection follows the Comté past the Roche Diamant setting, turns through the Cap Mocy/Mont Diablo bend and continues northeast by Roche Tablon toward Îlets Saint-Régis and the road crossing. The original map follows all these connected river reaches and separates the Nancibo and surrounding creek inflows from the selected trunk. No lake or reservoir transit is depicted.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Comté loop, joining river and transition to Oyak
correspondence.finding: The overlapping middle and lower originals show the selected lower Comté approach beside Pointe Maripa, the returning Comté loop and the southern/eastern incoming river connection, followed by the northward watercourse repeatedly labeled Rivière Oyak. The selected FID11514/11515 join lies on this connected receiving corridor. Its generalized line abbreviates the Pointe Maripa loop; the source supplies the actual connected river geography. The Orapu is independently identified as a separate Mahury-basin river in the hydrometric study and is not renamed Comté or adopted as the selected headward branch.

correspondence.component_scope: Oyak northward valley past Roura
correspondence.finding: The lower original repeatedly labels Rivière Oyak on the selected northward watercourse between the Maripa setting and Roura. It shows the complete sequence of bends beside Mont de la Cordelière and Montagnes de Roura, the separate short creek inflows, and the continuation past Roura. Oyak is a bounded reach identity, not an alias assigned to Brodel or the whole selected feature.

correspondence.component_scope: Tour de l’Île branch setting and lower Mahury
correspondence.finding: North of Roura the mapped river meets the distinct western Rivière du Tour de l’Île connection. The selected route continues on the broad north/northeast channel repeatedly labeled le Mahury, past the road crossing, Pointe Logoa and the Paramana-side margins. The western connection is visible but is not a separately selected tributary fragment. Adjacent wetland channels and the former Marianne polder drainage remain separate from the selected estuarine trunk.

correspondence.component_scope: Actual selected estuarine terminal
correspondence.finding: The lower original covers the entire selected approach and actual ending: the route turns east within the broad Mahury estuary south of Dégrad des Cannes and Pointe du Mahury. Its endpoint lies in estuarine open water before the farther seaward entrance. That actual ending is retained; it is not moved offshore or equated with a surveyed ocean-mouth point. The map supports the Mahury receiving-estuary identity and the river-to-estuary connection without a present tidal-flow, navigability or bank-side claim.

correspondence.component_scope: Interior icefield opening
correspondence.finding: The chosen eastern opening first runs west, dips south and returns northwest across a continuous snow- and ice-covered interior. The surrounding rock ridges and textured glacier surface are visible throughout. No open-water river or exact glacier-source name is demonstrated along this initial modeled line.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward and northwestward ice traverse
correspondence.finding: The next selected parts turn north and then northwest across the broad ice surface toward the western mountain margin. The bends and joins remain geographically covered; no separate tributary fragment is selected. This is ice-terrain correspondence, not proof of a natural surface or subglacial river following the model.

correspondence.component_scope: Ice-margin bends and rocky lake approaches
correspondence.finding: The route bends northeast and then north along a complex margin of exposed ridges, glacier tongues and narrow water-filled embayments before turning west into the larger lake setting. Several short selected intervals cross visibly rocky or ice-covered terrain rather than one demonstrated continuous river channel. The imagery resolves these land/ice/water settings; their mismatch with a uniform river interpretation is a feature-class limitation, not missing source coverage.

correspondence.component_scope: Broad lake passage and northwestern arm
correspondence.finding: The straight westward passage crosses the broad turbid lake, then the selection turns northwest along its arm beside a large rock island and the eastern valley wall. Hata and colleagues identify this intermediate waterbody as Lago Greve and describe drainage through its northwestern margin. That lake identity is contextual; it does not name the selected icefield-to-coast group.

correspondence.component_scope: Northwestern lake outlet and connecting valley
correspondence.finding: The selected corridor leaves the lake arm through a narrow exposed outlet valley and continues toward the next glacier-front waterbody. The intervening rocky narrows, stream and local joins are visible. Hata and colleagues describe a gorge and steep outlet stream connecting Lago Greve to a marginal lake of Glaciar Occidental. No precise historical or present channel position is imposed on the model.

correspondence.component_scope: Second lake and glacier-front margin
correspondence.finding: The route passes through the lower glacier-front lake and its western margin, beside a large ice tongue entering from the east, then reaches the lake outflow. These lake, ice-front and outwash settings are completely visible. The glacier label is not assigned to a selected exact point, and this lake is not treated as another name for the entire river group.

correspondence.component_scope: Braided outwash and actual coastal approach
correspondence.finding: The final selected parts continue northwest through a broad pale braided outwash valley between exposed hills. The actual rendered endpoint lies at the lowermost outwash/coastal-entrance margin, immediately beside the inner coastal water, rather than tracing the whole fjord onward. The ending and its neighboring channel bars are visible. No exact fjord name, tidal boundary, surveyed mouth or current preferred distributary is assigned.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen northern opening and eastward upper bend
correspondence.finding: The overview maps a small north-to-south wash at the selected opening, bending east along the northern side of the local hills and then entering the southbound eastern valley. The separately named Watson Wash passes to the west of those hills. The independent imagery visibly shows the dry wash gathering the opening gullies, following the eastward rock-margin bend and turning into the eastern valley.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern upper valley to Goffs turn
correspondence.finding: The chosen branch continues down the valley west of the Vonttrigger Hills and alongside Lanfair Road, then turns southwest near Goffs into the receiving valley. The mapped dry-wash network supplies ordinary corridor correspondence. The imagery corroborates the northern portion of this southbound valley only; the overview supplies continuation to Goffs.

correspondence.component_scope: Goffs–Fenner southwest corridor and Interstate40 collecting joins
correspondence.finding: The mapped wash continues southwest beside the Goffs road/rail corridor and merges with western wash channels near the Interstate40 crossing. Watson Wash is directly named upstream on that western contributing system. The selected eastern branch and its collecting joins are not assumed to share one name.

correspondence.component_scope: Essex and downstream Fenner Valley corridor
correspondence.finding: The overview shows the southwest collecting wash and entering side drainages beside the National Trails Highway and railroad, continuing along the valley between the Clipper/Marble side and the Old Woman/Ship Mountains. The independent county study identifies the wash adjacent to Essex as Watson Wash draining toward Cadiz Lake, without resolving whole-system nomenclature.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower alluvial approach north of Cadiz Lake
correspondence.finding: Below the rail crossing west of the Ship Mountains, mapped and visible wash traces spread across a continuous lower alluvial receiving fan. Imagery shows the selected western approach within the same fan and dune-margin setting meeting the northwestern Cadiz playa lobe. There is no observed intervening divide or separate corridor transfer. Regional map linework stops short of the lake, but the ordinary fan-to-playa entry is supported by the imagery together with the county destination prose. Absence of a distinct wetted thread is not a material gap.

correspondence.component_scope: Cadiz Lake receiving playa and final selected ending
correspondence.finding: Cadiz Lake is directly named and mapped as a dry lake. The imagery confirms the pale playa surface, its northwestern receiving lobe and the final selected ending within that lake setting, amid visible salt-working features. The preceding continuous receiving fan meets this lobe. No river trace across the playa floor is required.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen opening and eastward plateau ravine
correspondence.finding: The chosen opening lies in a broad pale dry ravine cut into the plateau. The selected route follows the ravine eastward, past successive side gullies and wider sandy reaches, to its eastward bend and turn into a southward valley. The opening, all six stored parts and their internal joins are covered by the original imagery. The orientation line is not used as naming or channel evidence.

correspondence.component_scope: Southward upper valley and its side-gully joins
correspondence.finding: A continuous broad dry-channel valley runs south and then southeast beside dissected plateau margins. Numerous side gullies enter it. The selected turn and internal joins correspond to this visible valley corridor; overlapping upper and middle views cover both sides of the transition. No intervening lake or reservoir is visible at the inspected scale.

correspondence.component_scope: Middle valley bends and larger tributary junction
correspondence.finding: The pale alluvial channel continues southeast between eroded plateau edges, bends south at a larger side-valley junction, then curves around a projecting plateau spur. The visible junction and all four selected parts are covered. Side-valley names remain unestablished; no neighboring label is applied to them.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower confined valley and road-crossed approach
correspondence.finding: The dry channel turns southeast along the foot of the plateau and receives additional side gullies before the lower open plain. Its sandy channel belt remains visible through the bends and across a road crossing. No reservoir impoundment or separate managed-channel transfer is needed to explain this ordinary corridor correspondence. No engineering or present operational condition is inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Valley exit, sandy fan and southern fan-to-playa entry
correspondence.finding: At the valley exit, the formerly confined sandy channel spreads into a branching alluvial fan. A conspicuous branch trends east, while the selected southern continuation occupies the adjoining pale, partly vegetated fan with shallow distributary and wash traces. The detailed view covers this entire transition across the road-cut fan into the smoother playa floor. The fan is partly masked by sandy hummocks and vegetation, so no continuously active wetted thread or exact modern bank is asserted. This is geographic fan-entry correspondence rather than a transfer across an unseen divide.

correspondence.component_scope: Playa continuation, final northeastward bend and actual ending
correspondence.finding: The final stored parts continue within the same broad low-gradient playa and its marginal flats, first southeast and then northeast into a darker patch on the playa floor. The whole bend, actual selected ending and surrounding receiving basin are visible in the terminal view, including nearby pale salt-crusted surfaces and minor marginal pools. No distinct channel across every part of the saline floor is claimed or required. The receiving depression is kept separate from any natural-river identity, and neither the depression nor the selected ending receives an established name here.
